tools.name: emit_signal
tools.description: Emit a signal to the sajou scene. Call this to animate the scene in response to agent events. Signals trigger any choreography wired to their type — the animation plays automatically. Call get_choreographies first to see what signal types are already wired. Well-known signal types and their required payload fields: task_dispatch (taskId, from, to, description?), tool_call (toolName, agentId, callId?, input?), tool_result (toolName, agentId, success, callId?, output?), agent_state_change (agentId, from, to) — states: idle|thinking|acting|waiting|done|error, error (message, severity) — severity: warning|error|critical, completion (taskId, success, agentId?, result?), text_delta (agentId, content), thinking (agentId, content), token_usage (agentId, promptTokens, completionTokens, model?, cost?). Custom signal types (any string) are also valid.

type.description: Signal type. Well-known: task_dispatch, tool_call, tool_result, token_usage, agent_state_change, error, completion, text_delta, thinking. Custom types are also accepted.

from.description: Entity ID of the signal sender (e.g. 'orchestrator', 'agent-1').

to.description: Entity ID of the signal receiver, if applicable.

payload.description: Additional payload data for the signal.

tools.name: get_scene_state
tools.description: Get the full state of the sajou scene — entities, positions, topology, layers, and editor mode. Use this when you need complete spatial context: entity positions, scene dimensions, routes, layers. For just getting actor IDs and states, list_entities is lighter. For a human-readable overview including choreographies and wiring, use describe_scene. Returns: all entities with id, semanticId, entityType, position, visibility, and layer.

tools.name: get_choreographies
tools.description: List all choreographies in the current scene with their trigger signal types and wiring. Call this before emit_signal to know which signal types will produce animations. If a signal type you want to use has no wired choreography, create one with create_choreography then connect it with map_signals. Returns: choreography ID, trigger signal type, step count, step action types, and wired signal sources.

tools.name: list_themes
tools.description: List available sajou themes. NOTE: Theme catalog is under development. Use get_scene_state and get_choreographies to interact with the currently loaded scene instead.

tools.name: get_catalog
tools.description: Get the entity catalog for a theme. NOTE: Theme catalog is under development. Use get_scene_state to see entities in the currently loaded scene instead.

theme.description: Theme ID to get the catalog for.

tools.name: map_signals
tools.description: Wire a signal type to a choreography — when that signal type arrives, the choreography plays. Call this after create_choreography to activate it. This is the simplest wiring method. Use this for: one signal type → one choreography (most common case). Use create_wire instead for: filtering by signal source, fan-out to multiple choreographies, or manual patch-bay control. Example: map_signals({signalType:'tool_call', choreographyId:'choreo-tool-call'}) — every tool_call signal now triggers that choreography.

signal_type.description: The signal type to listen for (e.g. 'task_dispatch', 'tool_call', 'error').

choreography_id.description: The choreography ID to trigger when the signal arrives.

tools.name: describe_scene
tools.description: Get a comprehensive, human-readable description of the current sajou scene. ALWAYS call this first before any other tool — it gives you the full picture: placed entities (actors), choreographies and their trigger signals, signal sources, bindings, and wiring. Use the returned semanticIds to target entities in subsequent calls. If the scene is empty, use get_catalog to see available entity types, then place_entity.

tools.name: place_entity
tools.description: Place an entity on the scene. Call this to add a visual actor that can be animated. Always assign a semanticId to actors you want choreographies to target by name. entityType must match a type from the theme catalog (use get_scene_state to see what's loaded; common types: 'peon' for humanoid agents, 'pigeon' for messages, 'forge'/'barracks' for locations). Example: place_entity({entityType:'peon', semanticId:'agent-1', position:{x:400,y:300}}) — then set_entity_state('agent-1','walk') or reference 'agent-1' in choreography steps.

entityId.description: The entity type ID from the theme catalog (e.g. 'peon', 'tree', 'building-townhall'). Use get_catalog to list available entity types.

x.description: X position on the scene (pixels from left). Scene is typically 960px wide.

y.description: Y position on the scene (pixels from top). Scene is typically 640px tall.

semanticId.description: Optional actor name for this entity (e.g. 'agent-1', 'door-kitchen', 'indicator-status'). When set, choreographies can target this entity by name. Must be unique across all placed entities. Omit for passive decoration entities.

scale.description: Uniform scale factor. 1 = normal size, 0.5 = half, 2 = double. Defaults to 1.

zIndex.description: Z-order within the layer. Higher values render on top. Defaults to 0.

tools.name: create_choreography
tools.description: Create a choreography — a named sequence of animation steps triggered by a signal type. Use this when you want agent events to automatically trigger animations. Workflow: create_choreography → then call map_signals (simple) or create_wire (advanced) to connect it. Available step actions: move (animate to position), fly (arc movement), flash (color highlight), spawn (create entity), destroy (remove entity), wait (pause Nms), setAnimation (change state), parallel (run steps concurrently), onArrive (chain after movement), onInterrupt (handle cancellation). Minimal example — tool_call moves agent-1 to workstation then back: steps: [{action:'move',entity:'agent-1',to:{x:700,y:250},duration:800}, {action:'flash',target:'agent-1',color:'#00ccff'}, {action:'move',entity:'agent-1',to:{x:400,y:300},duration:600}]

on.description: Signal type that triggers this choreography (e.g. 'tool_call', 'agent_state_change', 'task_dispatch'). This is the default trigger — the actual wiring is done via create_wire.

action.description: The animation action to perform. 'move' — animate entity along a path to target position. 'fly' — instant arc movement to target. 'flash' — brief visual highlight on the entity. 'spawn' — create a new entity instance at a position. 'destroy' — remove an entity from the scene. 'wait' — pause the sequence for a duration. 'playSound' — trigger an audio cue. 'setAnimation' — change the entity's animation state (e.g. 'idle' → 'walk'). 'parallel' — run child steps simultaneously. 'onArrive' — execute child steps when entity reaches destination. 'onInterrupt' — execute child steps if choreography is interrupted.

entity.description: Target entity semanticId (e.g. 'agent-1', 'door-kitchen'). Can use signal references like 'signal.payload.from' to dynamically resolve. If omitted, uses the choreography's defaultTargetEntityId.

target.description: Target position or waypoint name for movement actions (e.g. 'workstation-1', 'patrol-route').

delay.description: Delay in milliseconds before this step starts.

duration.description: Duration in milliseconds for timed actions (move, wait).

params.description: Additional parameters specific to the action type. For 'flash': { color: '#ff0', intensity: 0.8 }. For 'setAnimation': { state: 'walk' }. For 'spawn': { entityId: 'arrow', x: 100, y: 200 }. For 'playSound': { sound: 'click' }.

steps.description: Ordered list of animation steps to execute when triggered.

defaultTargetEntityId.description: Default entity semanticId for steps that don't specify their own entity. Useful when most steps target the same actor.

when.description: Optional payload filter — choreography only triggers when signal payload matches. Example: { field: 'toolName', operator: 'eq', value: 'Read' } triggers only for Read tool calls.

interrupts.description: If true, this choreography can interrupt a running one on the same entity. Default: false.

tools.name: create_binding
tools.description: Create a binding between a choreography and an entity property. Bindings connect choreography outputs to entity visual properties (position, rotation, opacity, animation state, etc.). Example: bind a 'tool_call' choreography's output to agent-1's 'animation.state' property, so when the choreography runs, the agent switches to a 'working' animation. The binding specifies which choreography provides the data, which entity receives it, and which property is controlled.

targetEntityId.description: The semanticId of the target entity (e.g. 'agent-1', 'door-kitchen'). This must match a placed entity's semanticId in the scene.

property.description: The entity property to bind to. Available properties: 'position' (point2D), 'position.x'/'position.y' (float), 'rotation' (float, degrees), 'scale'/'scale.x'/'scale.y' (float), 'opacity' (float, 0-1), 'visible' (bool), 'tint' (color), 'animation.state' (enum — switches animation), 'animation.speed' (float), 'zIndex' (int), 'moveTo:waypoint' (event — move entity to a waypoint), 'followRoute' (event — entity follows a route), 'teleportTo' (event — instant move).

sourceChoreographyId.description: The ID of the choreography that provides the data for this binding.

sourceType.description: The type of data the choreography outputs. Defaults to 'event'. Must be compatible with the target property's accepted types.

sourceField.description: Specific field to extract from the signal payload (e.g. 'velocity', 'value'). If omitted, auto-detected from context.

mapping.description: Optional value mapping function. Example: { fn: 'linear', inputRange: [0, 100], outputRange: [0, 1] }.

action.description: Optional action config for event→action bindings. Example for moveTo: { waypoint: 'workstation-1', animationDuring: 'walk', animationOnArrival: 'idle', duration: 1000 }.

transition.description: Optional transition config for smooth property changes. Example: { targetValue: 0.5, durationMs: 300, easing: 'easeOut' }.

tools.name: create_wire
tools.description: Create a wire connection in the sajou patch bay. Wires define data flow through 3 layers: (1) signal → signal-type: connects a signal source to a signal channel, (2) signal-type → choreographer: triggers a choreography when that signal type arrives, (3) choreographer → theme: sends choreography output to the theme renderer. Example flow: wire 'local:claude-code' (signal source) → 'tool_call' (signal type) → choreography-id (choreographer). This means: when Claude Code emits a tool_call signal, trigger the choreography.

fromZone.description: Source zone. 'signal' — a signal source (e.g. 'local:claude-code', a WebSocket source ID). 'signal-type' — a signal type channel (e.g. 'tool_call', 'agent_state_change'). 'choreographer' — a choreography node (use its ID).

fromId.description: ID of the source endpoint. For 'signal' zone: the signal source ID (e.g. 'local:claude-code'). For 'signal-type' zone: the signal type name (e.g. 'tool_call'). For 'choreographer' zone: the choreography ID.

toZone.description: Destination zone. 'signal-type' — route a source to a signal type channel. 'choreographer' — trigger a choreography from a signal type. 'theme' — send choreography output to the theme renderer. 'shader' — connect to a shader uniform (format: '{shaderId}:{uniformName}').

toId.description: ID of the destination endpoint. For 'signal-type' zone: the signal type name. For 'choreographer' zone: the choreography ID. For 'theme' zone: the theme slot name. For 'shader' zone: '{shaderId}:{uniformName}'.

tools.name: remove_item
tools.description: Remove an item from the scene. Supports removing entities, choreographies, bindings, wires, and signal sources. For entities, you can pass either the instance id or the semanticId (actor name) — the tool resolves semanticId to the instance id automatically. Use list_entities, get_choreographies, or describe_scene to find item IDs. Removing a choreography also cleans up its connected wires. Removing a signal source also cleans up its wires.

type.description: What type of item to remove. 'entity' — a placed entity instance (use the instance ID, not the entity type). 'choreography' — a choreography definition (also removes connected wires). 'binding' — an entity binding. 'wire' — a wire connection. 'source' — a signal source (local sources cannot be removed).

id.description: The ID of the item to remove. For entities, this can be the instance id (UUID) or the semanticId (actor name like 'agent-1', 'door-kitchen').

tools.name: list_entities
tools.description: List all placed entities in the scene with their semanticId, current state, and key properties. Call this when you need a quick roster of actors before targeting them. Lighter than get_scene_state — use when you only need IDs and states, not full topology. Entities with a semanticId are named actors (e.g. 'agent-1', 'door-kitchen') — use their semanticId in set_entity_state, update_entity, get_entity, and remove_item. Entities without a semanticId are passive decoration and cannot be targeted by name.

filter.description: Filter entities: 'actors' = only entities with a semanticId, 'decoration' = only entities without a semanticId, 'all' = everything (default).

tools.name: get_entity
tools.description: Get the full state of a specific entity by its semanticId (actor name) or instance id. Returns position, visual state, properties, and any active bindings. Use semanticId for named actors (e.g. 'agent-1', 'door-kitchen'). Use id for entities without a semanticId.

semanticId.description: The entity's actor name (semanticId). Preferred way to target named entities.

id.description: The entity's instance id (UUID). Use when the entity has no semanticId.

tools.name: update_entity
tools.description: Update properties of an existing entity. Target by semanticId (preferred for actors) or id. Only provided fields are changed — everything else stays as-is. Use this for position changes, scale/rotation adjustments, opacity fades, visibility toggles, layer moves, and z-order changes. For just changing the animation state, prefer set_entity_state (simpler).

semanticId.description: Target entity by its actor name (semanticId). Preferred for named entities.

id.description: Target entity by its instance id (UUID). Use when no semanticId exists.

zIndex.description: New z-order within the layer (higher = on top).

tools.name: set_entity_state
tools.description: Change an entity's animation state immediately — no choreography needed. Use for direct, instant state changes: set_entity_state('agent-1', 'walk'), set_entity_state('door-kitchen', 'open'), set_entity_state('indicator-status', 'active'). Use emit_signal instead when you want the state change to be driven by agent events via choreography. The state string must match one of the entity's defined animation states. Use list_entities to see current states.

semanticId.description: Target entity by its actor name (semanticId). Preferred for named entities.

id.description: Target entity by its instance id (UUID). Use when no semanticId exists.

state.description: The new animation state (e.g. 'idle', 'walk', 'work', 'open', 'closed', 'active', 'off'). Must match a state defined in the entity's visual configuration.

tools.name: create_shader
tools.description:
Create a GLSL shader — a visual layer that renders custom fragment/vertex shaders on the sajou scene. Shaders are the most expressive visual primitive: they run per-pixel GPU code every frame.

**Uniforms** are the knobs the choreographer can tween. Declare them in the GLSL source and in the `uniforms` array so the UI and choreographer know about them. Each uniform has a control type (slider, color, toggle, xy) and value range.

**@object grouping**: Use the `objects` array to declare virtual objects (e.g. 'sphere', 'camera'). Then set `objectId` on uniforms to group them under that object in the UI. This is purely organizational.

**@bind semantic**: Set `bind: { semantic: 'intensity' }` on a uniform to connect it to choreographer signals. The choreographer can then tween that uniform in response to agent events.

**Multi-pass**: Set `passes: 2` (or more) for ping-pong feedback effects (e.g. reaction-diffusion, fluid sim). The previous frame is available as `iChannel0`.

**Auto-injected uniforms** (do NOT declare these — they are always available):
- `iTime` (float) — elapsed time in seconds
- `iTimeDelta` (float) — time since last frame
- `iResolution` (vec3) — canvas width, height, pixel ratio
- `iMouse` (vec4) — mouse position
- `iFrame` (int) — frame counter
- `iChannel0` (sampler2D) — previous frame (multi-pass only)

**Minimal example** — animated gradient:
```glsl
#version 300 es
precision highp float;
in vec2 vUv;
out vec4 fragColor;
uniform float uSpeed; // @ui: slider
void main() {
  vec3 col = 0.5 + 0.5 * cos(iTime * uSpeed + vUv.xyx + vec3(0,2,4));
  fragColor = vec4(col, 1.0);
}
```

After creating a shader, use `set_uniform` to tweak parameters in real-time, or wire it to the choreographer via `create_wire` (choreographer → shader).

name.description: Display name for the shader (e.g. 'Plasma Background', 'Agent Glow').

fragmentSource.description: GLSL fragment shader source code (ES 3.0). Must include #version 300 es, precision qualifier, and output to fragColor. Auto-injected uniforms (iTime, etc.) are available without declaring them.

vertexSource.description: GLSL vertex shader source. If omitted, a default passthrough vertex shader is used that passes UVs to the fragment shader via vUv.

name.description: Uniform name as declared in GLSL (e.g. 'uSpeed', 'uColor').

control.description: UI control widget. 'slider' for numeric, 'color' for vec3 RGB, 'toggle' for bool, 'xy' for vec2 position.

value.description: Initial value. number for float/int, boolean for bool, number[] for vecN.

min.description: Minimum value for slider controls. Default: 0.

max.description: Maximum value for slider controls. Default: 1.

step.description: Step increment for slider controls. Default: 0.01.

objectId.description: Virtual object ID this uniform belongs to (matches an entry in the objects array).

bind.description: Choreographer binding hint — connects this uniform to a signal semantic.

uniforms.description: User-defined uniforms exposed in the editor and available to the choreographer.

label.description: Display label in the UI panel.

objects.description: Virtual objects for grouping related uniforms in the UI.

passes.description: Number of render passes. 1 = single-pass (default), 2+ = ping-pong feedback.

tools.name: update_shader
tools.description: Update an existing GLSL shader. You can change the fragment/vertex source code, uniforms, name, or pass count. Only provided fields are updated — omitted fields keep their current values. Use get_shaders first to find the shader ID.

shaderId.description: ID of the shader to update (from create_shader or get_shaders).

name.description: Uniform name as declared in GLSL.

tools.name: get_shaders
tools.description: List all GLSL shaders in the current scene with full details: source code, uniforms (names, types, values, ranges, bindings), virtual objects, and pass count. Use this to inspect existing shaders before modifying them or setting uniforms.

tools.name: set_uniform
tools.description:
Set a uniform value on a GLSL shader in real-time. This is the primary way an AI agent controls shader visuals — tweak a float slider, change a color, toggle an effect, or move a 2D position.

The value type must match the uniform's GLSL type:
- float/int → number (e.g. 0.5)
- bool → boolean (true/false)
- vec2 → [x, y]
- vec3 → [r, g, b] or [x, y, z]
- vec4 → [r, g, b, a]

Example: to make a shader pulse faster, set_uniform({ shaderId: '...', uniformName: 'uSpeed', value: 3.0 }).

Use get_shaders first to discover available uniforms and their value ranges.

shaderId.description: ID of the shader containing the uniform.

uniformName.description: Name of the uniform to set (e.g. 'uSpeed', 'uColor', 'uInvert').

value.description: New value for the uniform. Must match the GLSL type: number for float/int, boolean for bool, number[] for vec2/vec3/vec4.
